mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the GDP growth is negative, or if the correlation between GDP growth and returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and a decrease in retail sales signals a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, which historically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing sector boosts economic activity.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% and RSAFS decrease > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment reacts negatively to the employment data.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index by more than 0.5% in a month signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates monetary tightening.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment and falling retail sales signals a weakening consumer demand environment, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increase > 0.3% and RSAFS decrease > 2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and RSAFS changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
